sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that Torah study must be a source of delight and vitality for the person, mirroring how the Torah is God's own delight, because through Torah study Israel and the Holy One become one.

translations.translation: And this is what they said:
"A person should always study in a place where his heart desires,"
for "desire" is a will that contains pleasure,
for although in Torah study there must also be the self-nullification of a servant
(the yoke of Torah),
and also the self-nullification of subjugation
(to review his chapter one hundred and one times),
nevertheless,
the main emphasis in Torah study is
that the Torah he studies should be his pleasure and vitality.
And one can give a reason for this:
since the matter of Torah study is that through it, Yisrael and the Holy One, blessed be He, become completely one,
therefore,
just as with the Holy One, blessed be He,
the Torah is the pleasure of the Holy One, blessed be He,
and "I was with Him as a delight"
so too must it be with the person who engages in Torah,
that the Torah he studies should be his pleasure.
[And even though the person's pleasure in the Torah he studies is from the aspect of its intellect,
as is also understood from the matter of "in a place where his heart desires,"
one can say
that in the inwardness of matters, his pleasure in Torah is because the Torah is the delight of the Holy One, blessed be He,
[and since Yisrael and the Holy One, blessed be He, are completely one,
therefore the Torah is also the pleasure of Yisrael],
except that in his revealed pleasure, he feels that his pleasure in Torah is from the aspect of its intellect].

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the two aspects of Torah—as related to mitzvos and as it is in itself—are hinted at by wheat (grain) and a tree, with the tree representing the higher aspect of delight.

translations.translation: And one can say
that the two aspects in Torah are hinted at in wheat and a tree.
For wheat, which is grain
[even according to Rabbi Yehuda it is only a type of tree],
hints at the Torah as it relates to mitzvos
(that Torah study is in order to fulfill the mitzvah of Talmud Torah,
and the like),
and the Torah as it is in itself is hinted at by a tree.
For the advantage of a tree over grain is
that grain
(even wheat)
is something necessary for a person's existence,
whereas the matter of a tree is that it produces fruits,
which are not necessary for a person's existence,
but rather are things of pleasure.
And furthermore,
even the sight of a tree
(not only eating its fruits)
causes pleasure,
as it is written:
"And He caused to sprout... every tree pleasant to the sight..."
And as is seen in practice,
that strolling in a garden,
a place where trees grow,
is a pleasure.
Based on this, one can understand the superiority of Rosh Hashanah for trees over Rosh Hashanah for vegetables,
even though vegetables include wheat
(human food)
which hints at Torah,
for the drawing down on Rosh Hashanah for vegetables is regarding the fulfillment of mitzvos,
and even the drawing down regarding the occupation with Torah
(wheat)
is regarding the occupation with Torah as it relates to the fulfillment of mitzvos,
whereas the drawing down on Rosh Hashanah for trees is regarding the study of Torah as it is in itself,
the matter of the pleasure of Torah.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that because the mitzvos are drawn from the Torah, the element of delight found in Torah is also drawn into the service of accepting the yoke in mitzvah observance.

translations.translation: And one can say
that since the mitzvos are drawn from the Torah,
and also that the fulfillment of mitzvos must be in the manner of the service of a servant is because the Torah said,
"And you shall serve the L-rd your G-d,"
through this, a semblance of the pleasure of Torah is drawn also into the service of accepting the yoke
(the service of a servant)
that is in the fulfillment of mitzvos.
And it is like the explanation in the continuation of 5666,
that this—that even a simple servant
[whose service is from the aspect of the master's yoke imposed upon him]
strives that the work he does should be for the beauty and glory of his master—
is because even a simple servant has pleasure in the work,
except that the pleasure of a simple servant is
[not from the aspect of the servant's own being and existence,
but on the contrary]
from the aspect of his self-nullification,
for since he has no independent existence, therefore the pleasure of the master is his pleasure.
And likewise in the service of G-d,
in the service of accepting the yoke there is also the aspect of pleasure,
except that the pleasure is the supernal pleasure.
And one can say
that this—that even in the service of accepting the yoke there is the aspect of pleasure—
is because even the service of accepting the yoke is drawn from the Torah,
for the Torah said, "And you shall serve the L-rd your G-d."
